messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: Streaming API p99 latency SLO breach in us-west-2 (SLO=750ms). Current p99=1.82s, p95=410ms. Alert: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/ALRT-3132 :rotating_light:
oncall-erin: grabbing this — seeing customer-facing errors reported. tagging @ryan_sre @maya_prodeng @ops_kim
ryan_sre: any signs of gpu saturation or kernel stalls? can you dump node metrics?
maya_prodeng: pulling metrics now. node host-gpu-04 shows prolonged iowait and writeback spikes. top 3 processes: acme-analytics (batch), model-server-prod (shared pool). iostat snippet:
```
Device:            tps    rkB/s    wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s %rrqm %wrqm r_await w_await aqu-sz  svctm  %util
nvme0n1           45.00   12000    45000    0.00   10.00   0.00  18.00   0.35   4.20   1.20   0.50  98.7
```
ops_kim: looks like the write KB/s is through the roof on host-gpu-04. that would explain streaming stalls (tail latency). acme-analytics started a heavy offline export ~20m ago per tenant owner logs.
tenant-owner-acme: yep, we kicked off a large parquet export at 17:12; didn't realize it would hit shared-gpu nodes. we're pausing it now. sorry about the hit. :grimacing:
ryan_sre: we should isolate that tenant immediately — move them off shared GPU pool to a dedicated spare pool and apply io throttle on the source node until migration completes. Can @ops_kim run move?
ops_kim: starting mitigation actions: 1) cordon host-gpu-04 2) evict acme pods with pod disruption 3) migrate acme to pool-dedicated-2 4) apply blkio throttle until migration finishes. running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon host-gpu-04
kubectl drain host-gpu-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
infra move-tenant --tenant acme-analytics --to pool-dedicated-2
sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.read_bps_device='8:0 50000000' /acme.slice
```
oncall-erin: noted, please post progress. I'll update status page and notify support. impact estimate: p99 breach affecting streaming clients, some reconnects.
deploy-bot: infra move-tenant job started: job-35721. logs: moving 6 pods, init draining.
monitoring-bot: metric update: p99 dropped from 1.82s -> 1.05s after cordon+evict (313210f10). p95 steady ~380ms. request error rate decreased from 0.9% -> 0.25%.
ops_kim: eviction completed, pods rescheduled to pool-dedicated-2. applying final blkio backoff for 5m while disk flush finishes.
ryan_sre: can we confirm GPU IO queue depth cleared and KV cache warm? any streaming stalls still?
maya_prodeng: GPU processors ok now, kernel writeback queue dropped to normal. KV cache hit ratio recovered to 97% for affected routes. streaming stall metrics: stall count fell to baseline.
tonent-owner-acme: thanks — export paused and rescheduled for off-peak. we'll follow up with quota increase request to avoid future collateral.
oncall-erin: drafting customer-facing summary: "We experienced a noisy-tenant IO burst in our shared GPU pool that caused elevated tail latency for streaming API calls in us-west-2 for approx 45 minutes. Root cause: large export from tenant acme-analytics causing device writeback spikes on host-gpu-04. Mitigation: tenant moved to a dedicated pool, temporary blkio throttle applied, affected node cordoned and drained, KV cache warmed. Current status: service restored, p99 at 210ms, p95 at 360ms. No ongoing error budget burn."
ryan_sre: created follow-up ticket INFRA-1459: add stronger noisy-tenant quota/auto-throttle and test cgroup throttling workflow. also add a dedicated alert for sustained node writeback > X MB/s to preempt.
ops_kim: quick note — blkio throttle command used during mitigation: sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.write_bps_device='8:0 20000000' /acme.slice. will document exact sequence in the postmortem.
deploy-bot: job-35721 completed successfully.
oncall-erin: handing off to @sam-night for overnight oncall; summary: incident resolved, temporary mitigations applied, follow-ups created (INFRA-1459, SRE-2372), customer notified. please monitor alerts and paging threshold for writeback alerts. :white_check_mark:
sam-night: taking over, thanks @erin. will watch for regressions and ensure follow-up tasks are triaged tomorrow morning.
ryan_sre: action items: 1) validate throttle works under load in staging 2) add early writeback alert 3) review tenant export quotas + UX 4) add 'noisy tenant' runbook (evict/migrate/throttle). assigning owners in the ticket.
oncall-erin: closing thread for live mitigation. postmortem draft owner: @maya_prodeng.
